title: Source-to-Synthesis Lag
dataSources: Reading progress (`reading:progress`), highlights (`highlight:capture`), note links (`note:link`), books finished (`book:finished`).
app: Reading and knowledge-management telemetry — Goodreads / StoryGraph libraries, Kindle highlights (Readwise), and note-graph exports (Obsidian, Notion) — streamed to Splunk HEC via APIs and scripted inputs.
spl:
index=personal (sourcetype=highlight:capture OR sourcetype=note:link)
| stats earliest(eval(if(sourcetype="highlight:capture",_time,null()))) as first_highlight, latest(eval(if(sourcetype="note:link",_time,null()))) as last_note by source_id
| where isnotnull(first_highlight) AND isnotnull(last_note)
| eval lag_days=round((last_note-first_highlight)/86400,1)
| stats avg(lag_days) as avg_lag_days, max(lag_days) as worst_lag_days
description: Measures the delay between capturing a source idea and integrating it into linked notes.
value: The longer raw captures sit untouched, the less likely they are to influence your thinking; synthesis lag keeps that honest.
implementation: Use a shared `source_id` between highlights and linked notes; measure time from first highlight to latest synthesis note.
visualization: Single-value panel with average and worst synthesis lag.
grandmaExplanation: It compares how long ideas sit around before they become part of your actual thinking system.
